title: Entity-Switched Datasets: An Approach to Auditing the In-Domain Robustness of Named Entity Recognition Models
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its findings focus on the performance disparities of NER models across different national origins, showing that models perform better on names from certain countries (e.g., American, Indian) and worse on others (e.g., Vietnamese, Indonesian), even within the same textual context.

measurement_description: The benchmark did not measure anything related to faith or religion. It measured the robustness of Named Entity Recognition (NER) models by evaluating performance differences when named entities were switched with plausible names from different national origins.
